protein-overload-hair: Protein overload is a buildup of protein on the hair strands that leaves them stiff, brittle and lifeless. Healthy hair relies on a balance of protein and moisture to keep its elasticity and strength, so too much protein upsets that balance.
the-root-cause-of-scalp-inflammation-und: Scalp inflammation is the body's response to a problem on the scalp, and it often shows up as itching, flaking and discomfort. Common triggers include harsh hair products, poor diet, stress, allergies and skin conditions such as psoriasis or seborrheic dermatitis.
b-vitamins-hair-growth: Biotin, folate (B9) and B12 are the three most important B vitamins for hair. They belong to a group of eight B vitamins that support healthy red blood cells, which carry oxygen to the hair follicles on the scalp.
how-much-hair-is-normal-to-lose-in-the-s: Losing 50 to 100 hairs a day is considered normal, and some of that shedding shows up in the shower. How much you notice depends on your hair type, length, washing frequency and hair care practices.
bed-head: Bed head is the messy, tousled look some people wake up with after a night's sleep. It is often associated with volume, texture and a carefree style, and many people choose it for its relaxed, natural appearance.
mature-hairline: A mature hairline is the natural shift of the hairline slightly higher as people age, and it occurs in both men and women. It typically moves back by a few centimeters, may look more V-shaped, and is considered normal rather than a sign of an underlying health issue.
hair-structure: Hair has three main parts: the root, the shaft and the tip. The shaft is built from three layers, the cuticle, the cortex and the medulla, and each layer has its own function.
is-salt-water-good-for-your-hair: Salt water can add texture and volume to hair, but it can also leave hair dry and brittle. It draws water out of hair and scalp, which can raise natural oils in greasy hair, while too much exposure can damage the hair cuticle.
sunflower-oil: Sunflower oil is a light, non-greasy oil extracted from the seeds of the sunflower plant, Helianthus annuus. It is high in vitamin E, oleic acid and linoleic acid, and it has been used for centuries in cooking and skincare.
hair-weaving: Hair weaving is an extension technique that adds length, volume and style versatility by sewing in, bonding or clipping extensions onto your existing hair. Its main downsides are expense, ongoing maintenance and the time it takes.
horsetail-extract: Horsetail extract comes from the Equisetum arvense plant, which is best known for its high silica content. The plant also contains minerals such as potassium and manganese, and saponins, which are natural detergents that can clean and condition hair and scalp.
hair-damage: Hair damage comes mainly from heat styling, chemical treatments and environmental stressors, which can affect both the cuticle and the inner shaft. Heat styling can strip moisture from hair, leaving it dry and rough, with split ends and breakage.
calcium: Calcium is a mineral best known for supporting bones and teeth, and it is also linked to hair health. Beyond bones, the body needs it for muscle contraction and relaxation and for nerve transmission.
hair-volumizer: A hair volumizer is a styling product, sold as a spray, mousse or serum, that adds volume and thickness to hair. Its ingredients coat the hair shaft and lift hair at the roots, creating space between strands for a fuller look.
head-massage: A head massage stimulates the skin and hair follicles and increases blood circulation to the scalp. It also triggers the release of endorphins and oxytocin, natural chemicals that bring feelings of happiness and calm.
anagen-phase: The anagen phase is the active growth stage of the hair cycle, when follicles are busy producing new hair strands. During it, cells in the hair bulb divide rapidly and the shaft extends outward, which determines the length and thickness of your hair.
sea-buckthorn-oil: Sea buckthorn oil comes from the berries, seeds and leaves of the sea buckthorn plant, a hardy shrub known for its resilience in harsh climates. It has been used for centuries in traditional medicine, and its rich nutritional profile is why it is used in hair care.
spirulina: Spirulina is a blue-green microalgae that grows in both fresh and salt water. It is rich in protein, B vitamins, minerals including iron, magnesium and selenium, and antioxidants, and it is recognized as one of the most bioavailable sources of essential nutrients.
emollient: Emollients are ingredients that moisturize and soften the hair and scalp, and they are found in shampoos, conditioners and leave-in products. When hair lacks moisture it can become dry, brittle and prone to breakage, which is why emollients matter.
catagen-phase: The catagen phase is the short transitional stage of the hair growth cycle, between the anagen growth phase and the telogen resting phase. During it, hair follicles cease producing new hair strands and go through a brief dormancy.
essential-fatty-acids: Essential fatty acids are polyunsaturated fats the body needs but cannot make, so they must come from food. The two primary types are omega-3, found in fatty fish, nuts, seeds and plant oils, and omega-6, found in vegetable oils such as soybean and corn.
hair-elastics: Hair elastics, also called hair ties or hair bands, are small bands of rubber, silicone or fabric used to secure hair in ponytails, buns and braids. They work by gathering the hair and holding it together with tension, which makes many different styles possible.
ingrown-hairs: An ingrown hair is a hair that curls back or grows sideways into the skin instead of growing out of the follicle. It happens when follicles become clogged, can cause red, inflamed bumps, and may be influenced by shaving methods, tight clothing or certain skin conditions.
grape-seed-extract: Grape seed extract comes from the seeds of grapes, a byproduct of winemaking. It is rich in polyphenols, flavonoids and antioxidants, including linoleic acid, vitamin E and procyanidins, and its light, non-greasy texture suits various hair types.
riboflavin-for-radiance: Riboflavin, also called vitamin B2, is a water-soluble vitamin essential for energy production and cell function. It contributes to the making of amino acids and fatty acids, which are building blocks of keratin, the main protein in hair.
scalp-massage: Scalp massage supports hair health mainly by increasing blood flow to the scalp and hair follicles. It works by mechanically stimulating blood vessels to dilate, and the scalp, like any skin, benefits from good circulation, exfoliation and care.
avocado-oil: Avocado oil is derived from the pulp of avocados and is rich in vitamins A, D, E and B-6 and minerals such as magnesium and copper. Cold-pressed avocado oil, which is extracted without heat, retains the most nutrients.
baobab-oil: Baobab oil is a cold-pressed oil from the seeds of the baobab tree, a species native to the African savannahs. Cold pressing preserves the oil's natural nutrients, and the oil is rich in vitamins, antioxidants and fatty acids.
omega-3-fatty-acids: Omega-3 fatty acids are essential fats you must get from your diet because the body cannot make them. The three main types are ALA, found mainly in plants, and EPA and DHA, which are found primarily in certain fish.
synthetic-hair: Synthetic hair is man-made hair, used in extensions and wigs, that is created from synthetic fibers designed to resemble the texture and feel of natural hair. The fibers are heated, cooled and shaped into strands that closely mimic real hair.
dark-strawberry-blonde-hair: Dark strawberry blonde is a hair color that combines the light-catching quality of blonde with the warmth of red. It is characterized by depth and warm undertones, which give it a rich but subdued look.
tocotrienols: Tocotrienols are members of the vitamin E family, known for antioxidant properties stronger than those of the more familiar tocopherols. They come in four variants, alpha, beta, gamma and delta, found in foods such as annatto seeds, palm oil and rice bran oil.
hair-texture-types: Hair texture describes how your hair feels to the touch and how it looks, based on the thickness of individual strands and the overall pattern. Hair can be fine or coarse, and straight, wavy, curly or kinky.
sacha-inchi-oil: Sacha inchi oil comes from the seeds of the Plukenetia volubilis plant, native to South America's tropical rainforests. It is high in omega-3, omega-6 and omega-9 fatty acids and rich in vitamins A and E.
brahmi: Brahmi, or Bacopa monnieri, is a small creeping herb that grows in wetlands and has long been used in Ayurvedic medicine. It is also called the herb of grace, and it is renowned in Ayurveda for its cognitive-enhancing properties.
quinoa-extract: Quinoa extract is derived from the quinoa plant, a grain crop whose edible seeds have been a staple food in South America for thousands of years. In hair care it is valued for its high protein content and its amino acids, vitamins and minerals.
probiotics: Probiotics are live microorganisms, mainly bacteria, that provide a health benefit when consumed in adequate amounts. They are often called good or friendly bacteria because they help maintain the gut microbiome.
hydrolyzed-protein: Hydrolyzed protein is protein that has been broken down into smaller molecules so that hair can absorb it more easily. It is a common ingredient in hair care products, known for adding volume, moisture and shine.
certified-trichologist: A trichologist is someone who specializes in hair loss, hair shaft problems and scalp conditions. Trichology itself is the branch of dermatology concerned with the health and disorders of the hair and scalp.
ceramides: Ceramides are lipids, or fats, found naturally in high concentrations in the top layers of skin, including the scalp. They form a protective barrier that locks in moisture and shields the skin from pollutants and irritants.
prebiotics: Prebiotics are non-digestible fibers that feed the beneficial bacteria in your gut. They are found in fruits, vegetables and whole grains, and unlike probiotics, which are live bacteria, they stimulate the growth and activity of those microbes.
is-good-circulation-important-for-health: Yes, circulation matters for hair growth because the scalp needs a constant supply of oxygen and nutrients from the blood. One study found thinning scalps have 40% less oxygen, though many hair researchers believe all scalps, even thinning ones, have ample blood circulation.
anti-dandruff-shampoo: Anti-dandruff shampoo is a hair care product formulated for dandruff, a common scalp condition marked by flakiness and itching. It contains active ingredients designed to target the root causes of dandruff.
vitamin-d3: Vitamin D3, also called cholecalciferol, is a form of vitamin D that the skin makes in sunlight and that also comes from certain foods and supplements. It supports many bodily functions, including the health and functioning of hair follicles.
hair-breakage: Hair breakage is when hair strands snap or fracture along the shaft, leaving shorter, weaker hair. Unlike hair loss, which is shedding from the scalp, breakage happens along the length of the hair and can show up as split ends, frizz or a brittle texture.
cysteine-complexes: Cysteine complexes are formulations designed to deliver the amino acid cysteine directly to the hair to reinforce its natural strength. Cysteine is especially abundant in keratin, the chief protein in hair.
hair-texture-chart: A hair texture chart helps you identify your hair type, from straight to coily, along with details such as strand thickness and moisture retention. To use it, wash your hair and let it dry without adding products so you see it in its natural state.
dermatologist: A dermatologist is a medical professional who specializes in diagnosing conditions of the skin, hair and nails. For hair concerns, they look for underlying factors such as genetics, hormonal imbalances, stress, diet and styling practices.
dead-hair: Dead hair is a term for strands that are irreparably damaged, since hair itself is not alive like skin. Heat styling, coloring and sun exposure harm the cuticle, which leaves hair weak, brittle and dull.
trichoscopy: Trichoscopy, also called scalp dermoscopy, is a non-invasive procedure that examines the scalp and hair with a device called a trichoscope. It magnifies the scalp up to 200 times, revealing details that are not visible to the naked eye.
how-to-thicken-hair: The first step in thickening hair at home is to assess its current state, including any signs of thinning. Taking good care of your hair, eating the right foods and handling it gently can all help it look and feel fuller.
almond-oil: Almond oil is a natural oil from the kernels of sweet almonds, rich in vitamins E and A, omega-3 fatty acids and zinc. It is lightweight and easily absorbed, which makes it a moisturizer for both hair and skin.
flaxseed-oil: Flaxseed oil, also known as linseed oil, comes from the seeds of the flax plant, Linum usitatissimum. The seeds contain dietary fiber, lignans and alpha-linolenic acid, an omega-3 fatty acid.
keratin: Keratin is a fibrous structural protein that is a main building block of hair, skin and nails. In hair it helps maintain strength and resilience and acts as a protective barrier against damage from the environment and styling products.
coconut-oil: Coconut oil comes from the kernel of mature coconuts and is made up mostly of saturated fats such as lauric acid. Those fats have a high affinity for hair proteins and penetrate deeply into the hair shaft.
collagen: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the body and a key component of connective tissue, giving skin its elasticity and resilience. Its triple-helix structure supports tissues, hair included, and collagen surrounds each hair follicle.
glutathione-for-gray-hair: Glutathione plays a real, specific role in the biology of graying hair. Aging follicles generate small amounts of hydrogen peroxide, and in young follicles the enzymes catalase and glutathione peroxidase clear it almost immediately.
jojoba-oil: Jojoba oil is extracted from the seeds of the jojoba plant, Simmondsia chinensis, and is technically a wax ester. It closely resembles human sebum, so it is easily absorbed by the scalp and hair without leaving a greasy residue.
hair-thinning: Hair thinning is a noticeable reduction in hair volume and thickness, and it can happen gradually or suddenly. It is often linked to genetics, hormonal imbalances, nutritional deficiencies and lifestyle choices.
biotin-vs-collagen: Biotin, also called vitamin B7, supports healthy hair, skin and nails, while collagen is a structural protein that provides support to skin, hair and nails. Which one suits you depends on what you want from your beauty routine.
does-wearing-a-hat-cause-hair-loss: No, wearing a hat does not directly cause hair loss. Hair loss is mostly influenced by internal factors such as genetics and hormonal changes, although a tight hat worn for a long time may cause temporary breakage.
